title: Grateful Dead Live at Eastown Theater on 1971-10-24

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1971 show highlighted by a soaring Dark Star and tight, inspired playing from the entire band.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised as clean, crisp and spacious – a classic sound‑board source that lets every nuance shine.  The concert itself bursts with kinetic energy, featuring a smoking Dark Star, punchy Garcia riffs on El Paso, and vibrant contributions from Keith Godchaux, Phil Lesh and Bill Kreutzmann, making it a standout performance of the early‑'71 era.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive 5‑star comments focus on both superb soundboard quality and a high‑energy, musically rich show; no substantive criticisms were noted.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers describe the audio as clean, crisp, spacious and much clearer than balcony recordings – no drop‑outs or muddiness reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set is praised for its seamless flow and relentless drive, with new material and the fresh keyboard presence adding excitement throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s playing is described as fleet, nimble, with perfect tone (Alligator Strat speculation) and stellar licks throughout the Dark Star and other numbers.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh delivers "body‑shaking" bass runs, powerful backing vocals on songs like Mexico City Sunset and provides a solid harmonic foundation.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir is noted for strong vocal moments (e.g., “Thank You, Friends”) and energetic rhythm work on tracks such as Jack Straw and Tennessee Jed.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux’s early‑stage high‑energy contributions are highlighted; reviewers note the fresh piano adds a new vibe to the 1971 material.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann is praised for aggressive, “punching the gas pedal” drumming that drives the second half, especially during the Dark Star climax.
